brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A Japanese black tea made and sold by the JA Minami Shinshu cooperative from Yabukita leaf grown around Iida in Nagano. The name is local dialect for roughly "it really is delicious".

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: It was developed to give a use to second-flush leaf, which is cheap and which most growers discarded, and went on sale in September 2003. With domestic black tea scarce, it became a local speciality known as the black tea of the Southern Alps, and a bottled version followed in 2008.
processing: Typical of black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
appearance_dry: Usually dark twisted leaf, sometimes with golden tips.
taste_profile: Low in astringency and rich in sweetness, easy to drink plain and unsugared.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
